item.title: Cloudflare One, Access - Automatically retrieve SAML IdP signing certificates
item.description:
Cloudflare Access can retrieve signing certificates from a SAML identity provider's metadata endpoint. Your IdP can publish replacement certificates without requiring you to upload each one to Access.

In your generic SAML identity provider configuration, set Signing certificate source to Fetch certificates from IdP metadata and enter the IdP metadata URL. The endpoint must return SAML metadata XML over public HTTPS, without authentication or redirects. It must not return a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS).

For API configurations, use metadata_url instead of manual certificate fields:

Access caches the certificates and does not poll the endpoint.

Removing a compromised certificate from metadata does not immediately revoke the cached certificate or existing Access sessions. For setup, planned rotation, and emergency replacement guidance, refer to Discover IdP signing certificates.

item.title: Cloudflare One Appliance, Cloudflare One, Cloudflare WAN - Configure a separate WAN gateway for each appliance in a high availability site
item.description:
You can now give each Cloudflare One Appliance in a high availability (HA) site its own default gateway on a static WAN. Before this change, both appliances in an HA pair shared the same WAN gateway. Now each appliance can connect to its own Internet circuit, such as a different ISP for each appliance, with its own static IP and gateway.

  • In the dashboard, when you configure a static WAN on an HA site, enter the secondary appliance's gateway in the new Secondary gateway address field, next to Primary gateway address.
  • In the API, set static_addressing.secondary_gateway_address when you create or update a WAN. To remove the value with a PATCH request, set it to null.

The field is optional. If you leave it blank, the secondary appliance uses the primary gateway address, which matches how HA sites worked before. You can only use this field on sites in HA mode.

For details, refer to About high availability configurations.

item.title: Risk Score - Investigate user risk events in a timeline
item.description:
User Risk Scoring now groups risk behavior instances in a timeline. Each group highlights its trigger and shows later detections in time order.

Customize the date range to focus on the events you want to investigate. Select a timeline marker to view its events. The sequence helps security teams follow how risk events relate during investigations.

Switch to Table to return to the existing table view whenever you prefer.

User Risk Scoring is available on Enterprise plans.

For more information, refer to User risk score.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Gateway - Cloudflare One adds Periodic Beaconing Traffic detection
item.description:
Cloudflare One now includes Periodic Beaconing Traffic as a risk behavior. It analyzes Gateway HTTP traffic for regular check-ins to the same destination.

Cloudflare flags a user after more than 30 contacts to the same destination in six hours. Contacts must be evenly spaced, from 10 seconds to about 12 minutes apart. Few other users in your organization contact that destination.

Detection uses traffic behavior only. It does not use threat intelligence, categories, or reputation. Malware can check in with a command-and-control (C2) server this way, but legitimate software also checks in regularly. Treat each event as a lead to investigate, not proof that a destination is C2.

By default, the behavior is off and its risk level is Info. To turn it on, go to Risk score > Risk behaviors. Cloudflare reports a continuing beacon once. Events usually arrive 3 to 6 hours after the six-hour window closes.

Periodic Beaconing Traffic is available on Enterprise plans.

item.title: Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel for SASE - Cloudflare Tunnel extends URL normalization
item.description:
Starting from version 2026.11.0, Cloudflare Tunnel extends the URL normalization introduced in 2026.10.0. Normalization now handles semicolon-delimited path parameters before matching ingress rules. This improves security for tunnels with rules that require Cloudflare Access validation. The URL path sent to your origin stays the same.

Starting 2027-02-08, new cloudflared releases will turn on URL normalization by default. This replaces the previously announced date of 2027-01-25, giving you time to test the updated behavior. Upgrade to version 2026.11.0 or later and test your path-based routing before that date, including rules that match paths containing semicolons. Configurations without rules requiring Access validation are unaffected.

This setting is currently off by default. To turn it on, run:

Alternatively, set TUNNEL_DISABLE_PATH_NORMALIZATION=false on each cloudflared replica and restart it.

For more information, refer to ingress matching and Access validation at the origin.

item.title: Access, Cloudflare One - GitHub automatically detects leaked Access service tokens
item.description:
GitHub secret scanning automatically detects Cloudflare Access service token secrets exposed in public repositories and reports them to Cloudflare. Access then disables the affected token and emails account administrators.

Other secret scanning tools can identify Access service tokens using their consistent Client Secret format: cfast_, followed by 40 alphanumeric characters and an eight-character hexadecimal checksum. For tools that support custom detection rules, use this regular expression to find possible secrets:

This pattern applies to Client Secrets created on or after August 26, 2026, not legacy 64-character hexadecimal secrets. Matching the pattern does not validate the checksum or confirm that the secret is active. For details, refer to Client Secret format.

Recover a leaked service token

Before you can re-enable a leaked token, you must rotate its secret.

Leaked secrets do not support a rotation grace period. When you rotate one, the previous secret is discarded immediately. Update your services with the new secret, then re-enable the token.

For API rotations, omit previous_client_secret_expires_at. A future expiration returns 400. Attempting to re-enable the token before rotation returns 409.

For recovery steps and leak metadata fields, refer to Recover a leaked service token.

item.title: Cloudflare One Client - Cloudflare One Client for Windows (version 2026.9.2663.1)
item.description:
A new Beta release for the Windows Cloudflare One Client is now available on the beta releases downloads page.

This release includes the following highlights:

  • Added automatic endpoint selection for Global Acceleration. When Global Acceleration is enabled for an organization, the client connects to the Global Acceleration endpoints while the device is in the acceleration region and to the standard anycast endpoints otherwise, and reconnects when a network change moves the device between them without requiring action from the user. The Connectivity page shows which tunnel and API endpoints are in use, and users who are allowed to override the selection can choose endpoints in Settings.
  • Added protection against unauthorized modification or uninstallation of the Cloudflare One Client. When enabled, the user will be asked to provide an administrator-generated code when trying to uninstall the client, which will otherwise be blocked. Users, including administrators, also can no longer stop the client service, and attempts to authorize an uninstall with a code or token, whether accepted or rejected, are reported to Cloudflare.
  • Added a Diagnostics page to the client that shows the connection status and health, live tunnel and device metrics, network details and the results of DEX tests in one place. Users can run a speed test from the page that compares performance inside and outside the tunnel while the client is connected. The Troubleshooting tools button collects a full warp-diag bundle, or runs a captive portal test that briefly reconnects Wi-Fi, and saves the result to the Desktop, so users no longer need to run warp-diag from a terminal.
  • The client now shows a banner when the network limits the tunnel MTU to a degraded or critically low value. The banner clears when the MTU recovers or the client disconnects.

Additional changes and improvements

  • The client now applies tunnel MTUs between 1147 and 1199 bytes measured by Path MTU Discovery. Previously the client ignored these values and kept a larger MTU, which could drop larger packets on networks such as mobile hotspots while the client showed as connected.
  • When Path MTU Discovery is enabled, the client now accepts larger packets from Cloudflare instead of limiting them to the size it uses for its own outbound packets.
  • When Path MTU Discovery measures an IPv6 path MTU below 1280 bytes, the client now reconnects over IPv4 and keeps preferring IPv4 until the network changes. Previously the client could stay on a smaller tunnel MTU over IPv6 on networks where IPv4 supports larger packets.
  • Access reauthentication requests now trust certificates in the operating system's certificate store, so reauthentication works on networks that perform TLS inspection.
  • For Zero Trust deployments, the client now records a traceroute of the network path outside the tunnel when the tunnel degrades or fails to connect. warp-diag includes the same trace.
  • warp-diag now includes redacted copies of the deployed MDM files and the names, but not the values, of stored registration secrets. It reports a QUIC path MTU only when one was measured.
  • Added the MDM parameters mdm_file_debounce_secs (1–60) and mdm_file_unavailable_debounce_secs (0–300), which set how long the client waits before applying a changed MDM file and before acting on a missing or unreadable one.
  • Added the MDM parameters managed_network_probe_interval_secs (30–300, default 30) and managed_network_probe_count (0 disables probing, 1–10, or -1 to keep probing until a managed network is found; default 1). After a registration or network change finds no managed network, the client now rechecks, so a device doesn't stay on the default profile because of a transient connection failure. Set the count to 0 to keep the previous behavior.
  • Added the multicast network policy and MDM setting (allow or drop, default drop). When set to allow, the client sends traffic for multicast addresses through the tunnel instead of dropping it, for networks that use multicast ranges for other traffic.
  • In proxy mode for Zero Trust, the client now sends hostnames from HTTP/HTTPS and SOCKS5 requests to Cloudflare for resolution instead of resolving them on the device.
  • The Connectivity page now shows the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses assigned to the tunnel while the client is connected.
  • When the app cannot reach the client service, the home screen now says why (service not running, not accepting connections, not responding, or connection dropped and reconnecting). It shows an error code and a Learn more link instead of "IPC error".
  • The client now shows a notification when an administrator removes the user's selected virtual network, and shows a specific message when the user selects a virtual network that is no longer available.
  • The consumer client home screen now shows when the connection is post-quantum encrypted.
  • warp-cli target list now accepts --hostname to filter targets by one or more comma-separated hostnames.
  • DEX HTTP tests now send a default User-Agent that identifies the Cloudflare One Client when the test does not configure one.
  • Reduced CPU usage by the Windows Capability Access Manager service (camsvc) caused by the client's Wi-Fi queries.
  • Reduced the client UI's memory usage.
  • The client UI no longer starts WMIC or PowerShell processes to collect memory information for crash reports.
  • Fixed installs failing with error 1603 on devices with Windows App Control (WDAC) policies, because some files inside the installer's custom actions were not signed. All components of the installer are now signed.
  • Fixed the installer asking the user to close running applications during an upgrade, downgrade or uninstall because other programs loaded the client's Visual C++ runtime libraries through the system PATH. The client now loads these libraries from a private folder so that closing other applications is unnecessary.
  • Fixed reinstalling the same version of the client from its MSI removing the updater service, which stopped the client from updating.
  • Fixed the client window appearing blank or white after an upgrade, at sign-in, after waking from sleep, or after a display change.
  • Fixed the client UI freezing and no longer showing status updates after the device woke from sleep.
  • Fixed the client UI looking for one of its libraries in a directory that standard users can create before looking in the installation directory.
  • Fixed a local user being able to crash the client service by sending a crafted query to the local DNS resolver.
  • Fixed the client service restarting when a firewall update for captive portal detection stalled while the device was asleep.
  • Fixed the client service leaking handles to processes after they exited, which could leave those processes listed as running.
  • Fixed the client getting stuck in a disconnected state on Windows on Arm devices because leftover tunnel adapters were not removed.
  • Fixed Windows resetting the Wi-Fi adapter after sign-in or a Wi-Fi restart when the client's firewall rules in Exclude split tunnel mode blocked Windows network connectivity checks. The client now allows those checks.
  • Fixed the client missing some network configuration changes after the first change was detected.
  • Fixed the client being unable to connect after an upgrade, downgrade, and upgrade that switched between consumer and Zero Trust registrations. The client now clears the mismatched registration so the user can register again.
  • Fixed the client continuing to use the previous tunnel protocol after a key rotation for a protocol change failed. The client now retries the rotation the next time it connects.
  • Fixed service token enrollment failing when it ran shortly after the service token was created. The client now retries while the new token becomes available.
  • Fixed the client reconnecting repeatedly when Global Acceleration automatic endpoint selection was enabled on devices in the acceleration region, and fixed the client keeping its previous data center after the selected endpoints changed.
  • Fixed a hostname-based split tunnel entry not taking effect until the next reconnect after its firewall rule failed to apply.
  • Fixed the client service failing to start when a split tunnel address in mdm.xml had no prefix length. A bare IP address is now treated as a single host.
  • Fixed a single malformed element in mdm.xml causing the client to ignore the whole file. warp-diag now includes the file as written.
  • Fixed warp-cli dns fallback add accepting an empty domain, which sent all DNS queries to the local resolver instead of Gateway. Fallback domain and split tunnel entries are now normalized, so removing an entry matches regardless of case or a trailing dot.
  • Fixed the DNS proxy caching answers for longer than the TTL of a CNAME record in the chain.
  • Fixed warp-cli registration license reporting an error on slow networks even though the license was applied, which left the client registered to a WARP+ account it did not recognize.
  • Fixed warp-cli debug network showing an all-zero interface GUID.
  • Fixed Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) results being reported with timestamps offset from the actual time after the system clock was corrected.

Known issues

  • A Windows DNS client regression may cause connectivity check failures on systems containing large hosts files. While our client includes a mitigation for this issue, users may still experience reduced DNS performance and connectivity check failures.
  • After an administrator removes a virtual network from a device profile or changes its default network, the virtual network list in the client may continue to show the previous networks until the client is restarted. This is a display issue only: the device connects to the networks its profile allows, and selecting a removed network is rejected without changing the connection. The warp-cli vnet command shows the current list. This will be addressed prior to the next GA release.

item.title: Email security, Cloudflare One - Improved investigation search for Email security
item.description:
Email security now has a unified search bar for investigations. It replaces the Email Screener side modal and makes searches easier to refine.

Search with keywords or field:value filters. Autocomplete suggests filters and values as you type. Add terms and press Enter to refine results, or select From, To, Disposition, Status, or Threat type values in results. Narrow results with a date preset or custom range.

This feature is available to all Email security customers.

item.title: Access, Cloudflare One - Sign in to Cloudflare Access with passkeys
item.description:
Cloudflare Access supports passkeys as a login method for protected applications and the App Launcher. Users can sign in with a passkey saved on their device, security key, or password manager instead of entering a one-time PIN or configuring an identity provider.

Users verify their identity with an existing login method once before enrolling a passkey. Administrators choose which applications accept passkeys and can remove a user's registered passkeys. Access policies still determine whether a user can access an application.

For setup and enrollment instructions, refer to Passkeys.

item.title: Cloudflare One - Cloudflare One adds fast flux detection to UEBA
item.description:
Cloudflare One now includes fast flux detection as a predefined risk behavior for user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA). When enabled, detections contribute to a user's risk score.

Fast flux is a DNS technique that rapidly changes the IP addresses returned for a domain. Threat actors can use it to make malicious infrastructure harder to track and take down. Detecting it can help security teams identify potentially risky activity and investigate it sooner.

To turn on fast flux detection, go to Risk score > Risk behaviors in the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard.

Fast flux detection is available on Enterprise plans.

For more information, refer to User risk score.

item.title: Email security - Set expiration dates for Email security policies
item.description:
Email security now lets you set an expiration date when creating an allow or block policy. This helps you apply temporary policy changes without removing them manually.

After the selected date passes, the policy expires and no longer applies.

This feature is available to all Email security customers, regardless of plan.

item.title: Browser Isolation, Cloudflare One - Block data entry with Browser Isolation without losing search, copy, and zoom (beta)
item.description:
Isolation policies now support a third keyboard option in beta: Allow read-only actions. Previously, the keyboard setting was binary — allow all input or block everything. With Allow read-only actions, you can block data entry while preserving the built-in browser actions your users depend on.

In Allow read-only actions mode, users can still find in page, select all, copy, print, and zoom. All other keyboard input is blocked from reaching the isolated page. Copy and print remain subject to their own policy settings, so the controls compose instead of overriding each other. For example, setting the keyboard to Allow read-only actions and copy to Do not allow lets users search and zoom but prevents them from copying content.

To use this feature, set Keyboard to Allow read-only actions in your isolation policy settings. Via the API, set keyboard to enable_read_only_actions in the biso_admin_controls object with version set to v2.

For more information, refer to Keyboard.

item.title: Cloudflare Network Firewall - New managed rule to help mitigate CVE-2026-98432.
item.description:
Cloudflare Network Firewall has a new managed rule to help mitigate the Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-98432 ↗︎):

  • Rule name: Block CVE-2026-98432 ↗︎ traffic
  • Rule ID: 6a4df2bf984946a88c74b07349557e83

The rule is disabled by default. To use it:

  1. Go to Networking > Firewall Policies > Managed Rulesets.
  2. Enable the rule with action Log first.
  3. Review traffic that matches the rule.
  4. If the matching traffic is not expected for your environment, change the action to Block.

For more information on enabling managed rulesets, refer to Enable managed rulesets.

For more details about the vulnerability, including an agent assessment prompt and evidence sources, refer to the Cloudflare Radar Zero Wire briefing ↗︎.

item.title: Load Balancing, Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Mesh - Steer Cloudflare One users and private networks to the same endpoint with session affinity and hash steering in private load balancers
item.description:
Private load balancers can now keep each user on the same endpoint. This helps with applications that keep session state on a single server.

Two options are available:

  • Hash endpoint steering. In the dashboard, set a pool's Endpoint steering to Hash. Each user is mapped to an endpoint within the pool.
  • Session affinity. With the API, set session_affinity to ip_cookie on the load balancer. Each user stays on the same endpoint while it remains healthy and your pools do not change. Refer to Session affinity.

For traffic from the Cloudflare One Client, Cloudflare identifies the user by their device, so a user stays on the same endpoint even if their IP address changes. For other traffic, such as from a Cloudflare WAN site, Cloudflare uses the source IP address.

This works for endpoints reached through Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Mesh, and Cloudflare WAN. Affinity pins the endpoint, not the cloudflared or Mesh replica that carries the traffic.

To learn how private load balancing fits with your connectors, refer to Load balance private network traffic.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Access - Organize and authorize Access service tokens with tags
item.description:
You can now assign key-value tags to Access service tokens and use those tags to organize credentials or control application access. Each token supports up to five tags, such as environment: production or team: payments.

Add or edit tags when you create or update a token in the dashboard or service token API. You can search and filter by tag on the Service Tokens page. Tags also appear in Resource Tagging, where you can query them alongside other tagged resources.

The Service Token Tag policy selector matches valid tokens with an exact key-value pair. For setup instructions, refer to Tag service tokens and Authorize service tokens by tag.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Access - Inspect provisioned users and groups with the SCIM population viewer
item.description:
The SCIM population viewer lets you inspect the users and groups provisioned to Cloudflare One by each identity provider. You can check which resources Cloudflare has received without making API requests or opening a support ticket.

In Zero Trust > Integrations > Identity providers, select a user or group count in SCIM resources to open the viewer. You can:

  • Search users by username, email, name, or resource ID, and groups by name or resource ID.
  • Inspect resource attributes in formatted or JSON views.
  • View group members and compare Cloudflare and IdP resource IDs with provisioning logs.
  • Delete individual resources from the Cloudflare SCIM population when you have edit permission.

The viewer shows provisioned resources rather than provisioning event history. Use SCIM provisioning logs to investigate failed requests. Existing SCIM deprovisioning and policy behavior remain unchanged.

For dashboard instructions and API examples, refer to View SCIM users and groups.

item.title: Data Localization Suite, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare One - Cloudflare WAN supports regional Gateway HTTP inspection
item.description:
Cloudflare WAN traffic can now use a Gateway processing region with Regional Services. HTTPS traffic enters a Cloudflare data center (that may be outside the selected region) via an IPsec or GRE tunnel, or through Direct CNI, and remains encrypted until Gateway forwards it to the selected region for TLS decryption and HTTP inspection. This feature gives organizations control over where their sensitive traffic is processed, supporting their data sovereignty goals.

This feature requires unified routing. The processing region applies to Gateway HTTP traffic and does not apply to Gateway DNS or network policy processing.

Contact your account team to configure a processing region. For supported regions, configuration details, and limitations, refer to Data residency for Cloudflare One.

item.title: Data Localization Suite, SSL/TLS - View your data localization settings in one dashboard page
item.description:
The Cloudflare dashboard now includes a Data Localization Suite Overview, a read-only view of the data localization settings on your account. It shows your Regional Services, Customer Metadata Boundary, and Geo Key Manager settings in one place, so you no longer need to check several dashboard pages and APIs to see where your traffic is processed and where your logs and private keys are stored.

To find it, go to Application Security > Data Localization Suite, or search for "DLS" in the dashboard.

The Overview has a tab for each product:

  • Regional Services: regionalized hostnames (filter by region or zone), regionalized IP bindings, and regionalized Spectrum applications, each with its region.
  • Customer Metadata Boundary: whether the boundary is on, the region (US or EU), and whether out-of-region access is allowed.
  • Geo Key Manager: every custom certificate with a geo policy, with its hostname, zone, region, and status.

Each item links to the dashboard page where you change its setting, and each tab links to the product's documentation.

item.title: Access, Cloudflare One - Google Workspace SCIM user provisioning through generic SAML
item.description:
System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) is an open standard that synchronizes user identities between an identity provider and a service. For more information, refer to SCIM provisioning. Google Workspace is rolling out custom SCIM profiles in beta. Organizations with access to the feature can use Google's built-in provisioning service to send user updates and deprovisioning events to Cloudflare One.

You must use a generic SAML identity provider in Cloudflare One. The dedicated Google Workspace integration does not support SCIM. Configure a SAML app in Google, then enter the Cloudflare SCIM endpoint and secret in the app's autoprovisioning settings. Turn on Enable user deprovisioning in Cloudflare One to revoke active Access sessions when Google deprovisions a user. Google's configured deprovisioning delay still applies. Support for the existing Google Workspace OIDC client will be added once Google adds support for OIDC + SCIM.

Group membership is configured separately. Have the Google SAML app send a groups attribute to include the user's selected Google groups during authentication. Selecting groups as a SCIM provisioning scope does not synchronize group membership, Google is still adding support for this in their SCIM provider.

Cloudflare One users must first authenticate to Access or register a device with the Cloudflare One Client before SCIM updates can apply. Availability of custom SCIM profiles depends on Google's beta rollout.

For setup instructions, refer to Google Workspace (SAML/SCIM).

item.title: Cloudflare One Client - Cloudflare One Client for Windows (version 2026.9.1555.1)
item.description:
A new Beta release for the Windows Cloudflare One Client is now available on the beta releases downloads page.

This release includes the following highlights:

  • Added automatic endpoint selection for Global Acceleration.   • Added protection against unauthorized modification or uninstallation of the Cloudflare One Client. When enabled, the user will be asked to provide an administrator-generated code when trying to uninstall the client, which will otherwise be blocked.
  • The client now shows a banner when the network limits the tunnel MTU to a degraded or critically low value. The banner clears when the MTU recovers or the client disconnects.

Additional Changes and improvements

  • The client now applies tunnel MTUs between 1147 and 1199 bytes measured by Path MTU Discovery. Previously the client ignored these values and kept a larger MTU, which could drop larger packets on networks such as mobile hotspots while the client showed as connected.
  • When Path MTU Discovery is enabled, the client now accepts larger packets from Cloudflare instead of limiting them to the size it uses for its own outbound packets.
  • Access reauthentication requests now trust certificates in the operating system's certificate store, so reauthentication works on networks that perform TLS inspection.
  • For Zero Trust deployments, the client now records a traceroute of the network path outside the tunnel when the tunnel degrades or fails to connect. warp-diag includes the same trace.
  • warp-diag now includes redacted copies of the deployed MDM files and the names, but not the values, of stored registration secrets. It reports a QUIC path MTU only when one was measured.
  • Added the MDM parameters mdm_file_debounce_secs (1–60) and mdm_file_unavailable_debounce_secs (0–300), which set how long the client waits before applying a changed MDM file and before acting on a missing or unreadable one.
  • The consumer client home screen now shows when the connection is post-quantum encrypted.
  • The client UI no longer starts WMIC or PowerShell processes to collect memory information for crash reports.
  • Fixed a hostname-based split tunnel entry not taking effect until the next reconnect after its firewall rule failed to apply.
  • Fixed the client window appearing blank or white after an upgrade, at sign-in, after waking from sleep, or after a display change.
  • Fixed the client service restarting when a firewall update for captive portal detection stalled while the device was asleep.
  • Fixed the client getting stuck in a disconnected state on Windows on Arm devices because leftover tunnel adapters were not removed.
  • Fixed the client being unable to connect after an upgrade, downgrade, and upgrade that switched between consumer and Zero Trust registrations. The client now clears the mismatched registration so the user can register again.
  • Fixed the client UI looking for one of its libraries in a directory that standard users can create before looking in the installation directory.
  • Fixed warp-cli registration license reporting an error on slow networks even though the license was applied, which left the client registered to a WARP+ account it did not recognize.
  • Fixed Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) results being reported with timestamps offset from the actual time after the system clock was corrected.
  • Added the MDM parameters managed_network_probe_interval_secs (30–300, default 30) and managed_network_probe_count (0 disables probing, 1–10, or -1 to keep probing until a managed network is found; default 1). After a registration or network change finds no managed network, the client now rechecks, so a device doesn't stay on the default profile because of a transient connection failure. Set the count to 0 to keep the previous behavior.
  • In proxy mode for Zero Trust, the client now sends hostnames from HTTP/HTTPS and SOCKS5 requests to Cloudflare for resolution instead of resolving them on the device.
  • When the app cannot reach the client service, the home screen now says why (service not running, not accepting connections, not responding, or connection dropped and reconnecting). It shows an error code and a Learn more link instead of "IPC error".
  • Fixed Windows resetting the Wi-Fi adapter after sign-in or a Wi-Fi restart when the client's firewall rules in Exclude split tunnel mode blocked Windows network connectivity checks. The client now allows those checks.
  • Fixed the installer asking the user to close running applications during an upgrade, downgrade or uninstall because other programs loaded the client's Visual C++ runtime libraries through the system PATH. The client now loads these libraries from a private folder so that closing other applications is unnecessary.

Known issues

A Windows DNS client regression may cause connectivity check failures on systems containing large hosts files. While our client includes a mitigation for this issue, users may still experience reduced DNS performance and connectivity check failures.

For Zero Trust documentation please see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/ For Consumer documentation please see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/warp-client/

item.title: Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel for SASE, Cloudflare Mesh, Cloudflare One - 50,000 routes per account and Tunnels for Platforms
item.description:
Two changes make it easier to run Cloudflare Tunnel at scale.

50,000 routes per account by default

The default limit for routes is now 50,000 per account, up from 1,000. This limit covers CIDR routes and hostname routes for Cloudflare Tunnel and Cloudflare Mesh. The new limit applies to every account automatically, with no action required.

Published applications (public hostnames) are not routes and are not affected by this limit. Each tunnel supports roughly 5,000–10,000 published applications, depending on the size of its configuration. For details, refer to Published application limits.

Tunnels for Platforms

Every account includes 1,000 tunnels. With Tunnels for Platforms, you can now run more than 1,000 tunnels in a single account — for example, one tunnel per device, per end customer, or per development environment.

To buy additional tunnels, go to Networking > Tunnels and select Buy more tunnels in the Usage card. Additional tunnels are billed at $4.50 per tunnel per month. Enterprise customers can contact their account team for committed or usage-based pricing.

Go to Tunnels ↗

For pricing, limits, and best practices for managing large tunnel fleets, refer to Tunnels for Platforms.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Gateway - Application Library now supports custom applications
item.description:
Starting today, you can create custom applications in the Application Library and reference them in Gateway DNS, Network, and HTTP policies. You can define an application with hostnames, IP subnets, or both. Then, optionally add TCP or UDP ports or port ranges to restrict HTTP and Network matching.

This release also improves search and filtering in the Application Library, updates the interfaces, data, and metrics used to review applications, and makes it easier to select and manage applications in the Gateway policy builder.

For more information, refer to Custom applications and Applications and app types.

item.description:
Cloudflare WAN and Magic Transit IPsec and GRE tunnels now support BGP import and export filtering.

Create reusable filter profiles that specify an allow or deny action and a list of Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) targets with exact, more-specific, or prefix-length matching. Each tunnel supports one import filter and one export filter.

You can create and assign profiles through the dashboard, API, or Terraform. Profile changes apply without resetting the BGP session.

For configuration details, refer to:

  • Filter BGP routes for Magic Transit

item.title: Cloudflare One, Workers, Gateway - Gateway and Workers integration is now in public beta
item.description:
Cloudflare Gateway now integrates with Cloudflare Workers in public beta on all Zero Trust plans. You can use the Forward action in Gateway HTTP policies to run your own code on matching, permitted traffic without managing a separate proxy.

The Forward action lets you transform HTTP requests and responses, return a coaching page, or run background tasks such as Slack notifications and R2 captures. Your Worker receives the request and Gateway context, including connection metadata, user identity, and device posture when available.

Gateway handles the proxy connection, TLS decryption, and upstream routing. It evaluates HTTP request policies before Forward policies and inspects the final response before returning it to the user.

Gateway inspects the original request body before delivering it to your Worker. A body-inspection Block decision can interrupt the Worker.

To get started, deploy a Worker and configure a Forward policy, or adapt one of the Worker templates.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Access - Infrastructure applications support a configurable session duration
item.description:
Infrastructure applications now have a configurable session duration with a default value of 24 hours. You can set the session duration when creating or editing an infrastructure application in the dashboard or via the API.

When the session duration elapses, any active SSH connections through that application will be closed, and users will need to reconnect. Previously, infrastructure applications did not enforce a session duration limit. Sessions could persist beyond 24 hours in some cases, but were never guaranteed beyond 10 hours due to Gateway connection limits.

When a target matches multiple infrastructure applications, the shortest session duration applies.

For more information, refer to Session duration.

DNS64 synthesizes AAAA records from A records for IPv6-only networks. These networks require network address translation from IPv6 to IPv4 (NAT64).

Turn on Enable DNS64 for a location, or include an empty EDNS option 65051 in individual queries. Both mechanisms support UDP, TCP, DNS over TLS (DoT), and DNS over HTTPS (DoH).

The existing cf-dns-options: dns64 DoH header remains supported independently. DNS64 is off by default. Each mechanism independently requests synthesis.

item.title: Cloudflare One Client - Cloudflare One Client for macOS (version 2026.8.2100.0)

item.title: CASB - Detect organization-specific risks with CASB custom finding types
item.description:
Cloudflare CASB now supports custom finding types, giving security teams full control over the security conditions CASB detects across their SaaS and cloud integrations.

In addition to CASB's library of standard finding types, you can now write your own detection logic using Rego ↗︎, the open-source policy language from Open Policy Agent (OPA). Use custom finding types to match your organization's own thresholds and exceptions, such as flagging admin accounts without two-factor authentication, and get higher-confidence findings to act on.

Key capabilities

  • Write your own detection logic — Define exactly what CASB flags using Rego expressions evaluated against asset data from your connected integrations.
  • Target any supported provider and asset class — Scope a custom finding type to a provider (such as Google Workspace or Microsoft 365) and asset class (such as users, files, or groups), and apply it to all integrations for that provider or a selected subset.
  • Built-in validation — Select Validate to check your expression for syntax errors and schema issues before you create the finding type.
  • Inspect and duplicate standard finding types — Open any standard finding type to view its detection logic, then duplicate it as the starting point for a custom finding type.
  • Works with CASB policies — Use custom finding types in CASB remediation policies to send matching findings to Slack, ServiceNow, or any other webhook destination.

Get started

  1. In Cloudflare One ↗︎, go to Cloud & SaaS findings > Findings library.
  2. Select Create finding.
  3. Enter a name, description, and severity.
  4. Select a provider and asset class, then set the integration scope.
  5. Write your Rego expression and select Validate.
  6. Select Create finding.

CASB evaluates the custom finding type against assets as they are created or updated within the selected scope. Matching assets appear as posture finding instances under Posture Findings.

Learn more

  • Learn how to create and manage custom finding types in Cloudflare One.
  • Learn how to manage findings in Cloudflare One.
  • Learn how to create and manage CASB remediation policies in Cloudflare One.

CASB custom finding types are now available in Cloudflare One.

BGP peering exchanges routes dynamically between your devices and your Cloudflare virtual network routing table. You no longer need to update static routes manually as your network changes.

item.title: Access, Cloudflare One - New strict service token authentication setting for Access
item.description:
The strict service token authentication setting applies consistent behavior to requests made with service tokens. When the setting is on for a Zero Trust organization, Access handles requests with service token headers as follows:

  • If authentication or authorization fails, Access always returns 401 or 403 instead of redirecting the client to the login page with 302.
  • Only Service Auth policies can authorize the request. Access ignores Allow policies and any CF_Authorization cookie sent with the request.
  • Access does not return a CF_Authorization cookie to the client after successful authentication. Subsequent requests should continue to use service token headers.
  • Failed requests for recognized service tokens appear in Access authentication logs.

Zero Trust organizations created on or after October 5, 2026 have strict service token authentication turned on by default and cannot turn it off. Cloudflare recommends that existing organizations turn it on as well.

Organizations created before October 5, 2026 can configure the setting in the dashboard or through the API.

  1. In the Cloudflare dashboard ↗︎, go to Zero Trust > Access controls > Access settings.

    Go to Access settings ↗

  2. Under Manage service tokens, turn on Strict service token authentication.

  3. In the confirmation dialog, select Enable.

To turn off strict service token authentication, turn off the setting and select Disable.

To turn off strict service token authentication, set strict_service_token_auth to false.

For behavior and configuration details, refer to Strict service token authentication.

item.description:

This change applies to inline target tagging through the Infrastructure Access Targets API. Tagging resources through the general Resource Tagging API still requires the Tag Admin, Tag Write, or equivalent role.

item.title: Cloudflare Mesh, Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare One, Gateway, Workers VPC - Identify Mesh, Workers VPC, and Cloudflare Tunnel replicas in network logs
item.description:
You can now tell a person on a laptop apart from a Mesh node or an AI agent running on Workers, without matching on connector email addresses or Mesh IP ranges — and see exactly which Cloudflare Tunnel and cloudflared replica received each session.

Gateway network logs and Zero Trust Network Session Logs now identify two new kinds of traffic:

  • Mesh — Traffic sent from or delivered to a Cloudflare Mesh node. Previously, Mesh nodes were logged the same way as devices running the Cloudflare One Client, because Mesh nodes run the client in headless mode.
  • Workers VPC — Traffic sent by a Worker through a Workers VPC binding. Previously, Workers VPC sessions were not recorded in Network Session Logs.

Gateway network logs

To view these values in the dashboard, go to Zero Trust > Insights & Logs > Logs > Network logs, select Columns, and turn on Traffic Source and Traffic Destination. Both values also appear under Network query details when you open a log entry.

Network Session Logs

The zero_trust_network_sessions dataset, available through Logpush, includes the following fields:

Field Description
OnrampType How the session entered Cloudflare One. Values: CF1_CLIENT, MESH, WORKERS_VPC, MAGIC, OTHER.
Offramp Where the session was routed. Sessions routed to a Mesh node report MESH.
SourceName Name of the Worker that started the session. Only populated for Workers VPC sessions.
SourceID Stable identifier of the Worker that started the session. Only populated for Workers VPC sessions.
DestinationReplicaID The replica that served the session, such as a specific replica of a Mesh node or a cloudflared replica of a Cloudflare Tunnel.

For example, OnrampType = 'WORKERS_VPC' AND Offramp = 'MESH' returns every session where a Worker reached a service behind a Mesh node, and SourceName tells you which Worker it was.

Redeploy your Workers

SourceName and SourceID are only populated for Workers deployed after 29 September 2026. To include them for an existing Worker, redeploy it — for example, with npx wrangler deploy. No code changes are required.

See which tunnel and replica received a session

With DestinationReplicaID, you can now confirm which Cloudflare Tunnel and which cloudflared replica received traffic for a specific session. Combine it with the existing DestinationTunnelID field to trace a session to an exact tunnel replica — or Mesh node replica — when you run multiple replicas for high availability. The replica ID matches the Connector ID shown in the dashboard, so you can stream that replica's logs with cloudflared tail --connector-id.

Sessions logged before this change are not backfilled. For all available fields, refer to Zero Trust Network Session Logs.

item.title: Access, Cloudflare One - MCP server portals are now generally available
item.description:
MCP server portals are now generally available to all Cloudflare customers. A portal gives users one endpoint for approved Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Cloudflare Access logs tool, prompt, and resource activity.

Since the open beta, MCP server portals have added:

  • Gateway routing for HTTP logging and data loss prevention (DLP) scanning
  • Code Mode policies that control how portals reduce tool definitions and token use
  • Static OAuth client credentials for providers that do not support Dynamic Client Registration
  • Session management for reconnecting servers and changing authorizations from the portal

To create a portal and connect an MCP client, refer to MCP server portals.

item.title: Access - Authentication options for Google Workspace identity providers
item.description:
Google Workspace identity provider integrations now include prompt controls and device-scoped login hints in the Cloudflare dashboard and API.

Choose Google's default behavior, silent authentication, consent, or account selection. If silent authentication cannot use an active Google session, Access retries once with Google's default interactive flow.

Access can also send a domain-matched login hint. It sends the hint when one email from a previous Access login on the same device matches the Google Workspace domain.

For configuration details, refer to Google Workspace authentication options.

item.title: Gateway, Cloudflare One - Traffic Destination selector in Gateway policies
item.description:
Gateway HTTP and Network policies now include a Traffic Destination selector that identifies how traffic exits Cloudflare. This allows administrators to write policies that target specific off-ramp methods - for example, applying different rules to traffic destined for the public Internet compared to traffic routed through Cloudflare Tunnel or Cloudflare WAN.

Available traffic destination values

UI name API value Description
Internet internet Traffic to the public Internet
Cloudflare WAN cloudflare_wan Traffic through a Cloudflare WAN connection
Cloudflare Tunnel cloudflare_tunnel Traffic to a private origin through Cloudflare Tunnel
Cloudflare One Client device_client Traffic to another device running the Cloudflare One Client
Mesh mesh Traffic through a Cloudflare Mesh node

The selector uses the net.offramp.type API field in both HTTP and Network policies.

UI name API example
Traffic Destination net.offramp.type == "internet"

For more information, refer to HTTP policies and Network policies.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Cloudflare Mesh - Add Mesh participants with guided onboarding
item.description:
Cloudflare Mesh now makes it faster to add and manage participants from the dashboard. Select Add participant from Networking > Mesh to deploy a Mesh node or find the information needed to connect a client device.

The updated dashboard includes the following improvements:

  • More Mesh node deployment options — Install a node on Linux, Kubernetes, Docker Compose, or Docker CLI. The dashboard provides requirements, commands, configuration, and links for each method. Refer to Run Mesh in Docker / Kubernetes for container deployment details.
  • Client device installation guidance — Access platform-specific Cloudflare One Client installers, mobile QR codes, and your Cloudflare One organization name. Use the organization name to log in from the client after installation.
  • Unified participant management — View Mesh nodes and enrolled client devices in one table. Search devices, filter participants by type or status, open device details, and load additional results from each participant source. If one source fails, participants from the other source remain available while you retry the request.

You must still install the Cloudflare One Client, log in to your organization, and test the connection.

For complete setup instructions, refer to Get started with Cloudflare Mesh.

item.title: Access - Automatically manage inactive Access service tokens
item.description:
Cloudflare Access administrators can now automatically disable or delete inactive service tokens. Administrators can set an inactivity period from 30 to 365 days and choose what Access does when a token reaches that limit.

To be eligible for cleanup, a token must be older than the configured period, must not have successfully authenticated during that period, and must not be directly referenced by an Access policy rule. Cleanup runs gradually in the background, so eligible tokens may not be disabled or deleted immediately.

For configuration instructions, refer to Manage inactive service tokens.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Access - Private MCP server support for MCP server portals
item.description:
MCP server portals can now connect to MCP servers available only on your private network. The portal uses Cloudflare Gateway to reach private hostnames and IP addresses without exposing the MCP server to the public Internet.

Connect the server network to Cloudflare with Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Mesh, or another Cloudflare One connector. Configure a private hostname or CIDR route, then turn on Route traffic through Cloudflare Gateway when you add the server. OAuth authorization server endpoints, such as the authorization and token endpoints, must be accessible on the public Internet. If Cloudflare automatically registers the OAuth client through Dynamic Client Registration (DCR), the registration endpoint must also be accessible on the public Internet.

For setup instructions, refer to Connect a private MCP server.

Unified Routing improves the integration between Cloudflare One and the standard connectivity onramps supported by Cloudflare WAN. It is capable of many new features including Automatic Return Routing, BGP and custom client subnets.

We recommend Unified Routing for all new accounts.

For details, refer to Cloudflare WAN traffic steering and Magic Transit traffic steering.

item.title: Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel for SASE - cloudflared to deprecate 32-bit Windows and Intel-based macOS builds in 2027
item.description:
Starting in 2027, Cloudflare will deprecate 32-bit Windows and Intel-based macOS builds of cloudflared. After the deprecation takes effect, Cloudflare will no longer publish new cloudflared releases for either architecture.

Windows 10, the last Windows release to support 32-bit systems, reached end of support in October 2025. Apple has also deprecated Intel-based Mac computers. macOS 26 Tahoe, released in September 2025, was the final macOS release to support Intel-based Macs. macOS 27, released in September 2026, no longer supports them.

Focusing development on currently supported architectures allows cloudflared to align with operating system support and continue receiving updates on supported platforms. For available downloads and supported platforms, refer to the Cloudflare Tunnel downloads documentation.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Access - Access for Infrastructure now supports tagged targets and tag-based target criteria
item.description:
Access for Infrastructure now integrates with Resource Tagging. You can attach key-value tags to infrastructure targets and use them in access policies.

You can manage tags on targets inline when you create or edit a target or through the central Resource Tagging API. Cloudflare keeps tags in sync across both methods.

Infrastructure applications also support a target criteria model with include, require, and exclude operators. Each operator can match targets by hostname, tag, or both.

  • Include matches targets that have any of the specified values.
  • Require matches targets that have all of the specified values.
  • Exclude rejects targets that have any of the specified values.

For more information, refer to Add an infrastructure application.

item.title: Access - Require fresh authentication for SAML identity providers
item.description:
Cloudflare Access can now request fresh authentication from a SAML identity provider for every login. Turn on Require reauthentication in the Cloudflare dashboard, or set force_authn to true through the API. Access will then set ForceAuthn to true in signed and unsigned SAML authentication requests.

This option is useful when an application requires users to reauthenticate at the identity provider instead of relying on an existing identity provider session. The default value is false.

For configuration details, refer to Require fresh authentication at the identity provider.

item.title: Data Loss Prevention - Discover where sensitive data goes before you create a Data Loss Prevention policy
item.description:
Passive Detection for Cloudflare Data Loss Prevention (DLP) lets you learn from your Gateway traffic before deciding what to log or block. Discover the sensitive data types in sampled traffic, explore their destinations, and use the findings to build policies around your organization's needs.

The dashboard brings together detections from sampled HTTP request and response bodies. Select an entry to follow its detections over time, review destinations, and check policy coverage. You do not need a Gateway DLP policy to get these insights, and existing Gateway policies continue to apply.

Passive Detection is generally available. The detection entries available to your account depend on your Zero Trust plan.

To get started, refer to the Passive Detection documentation.

item.title: Browser Isolation, Cloudflare One - Improved iOS tap-to-type experience for Browser Isolation
item.description:
Browser Isolation has improved the tap-to-type experience for users on iOS devices.

Previously, Browser Isolation displayed a full-screen overlay with the message tap to type when users focused a text field. The prompt now appears inline over the focused text field, reducing disruption when users enter text in isolated sessions.

If the focused text field is too small to display the full prompt, Browser Isolation displays a keyboard icon in the center of the text field instead.

iOS users should tap twice to begin entering text. This update applies automatically to Browser Isolation sessions on iOS.

For more information on why this interaction is required, refer to iOS limitations.

item.title: CASB - New CASB integration for Zoom
item.description:
Cloudflare CASB now integrates with Zoom. The integration connects through Cloudflare's pre-built OAuth application — no manual app setup in Zoom is required. After an initial scan, CASB continuously scans your Zoom account to surface new findings as your environment changes.

Zoom is widely used for meetings, webinars, and collaboration. Misconfigurations in account settings, meeting security controls, and recording access can expose organizations to data leakage, unauthorized access, and compliance risk. Cloudflare CASB ingests Zoom account data via API to surface security findings across these areas.

Key capabilities

Starting today, security teams can scan for security findings across the following assets:

  • Account settings — Detect weak password policies, unlocked security controls, and two-factor authentication gaps across your Zoom account
  • User accounts — Identify users not enforcing SSO, accounts with insecure host keys, unverified or inactive users, and unsafe overrides of account-level security settings
  • Meetings — Surface meetings without passwords or waiting rooms, meetings using Personal Meeting IDs (PMIs), and meetings with external domain hosts
  • Recordings — Detect publicly accessible cloud recordings, recordings without passcodes, and weak recording password configurations
  • Content — Identify sensitive information in meeting and recording content via DLP Profile matching

Learn more

This integration is available to all Cloudflare Zero Trust customers today. New customers can sign up and start with their first two integrations for free. Existing customers can enable the integration directly in the Cloudflare One dashboard under Cloud & SaaS findings > Integrations. The integration begins scanning immediately and surfaces findings in the dashboard within minutes.

item.title: Cloudflare One Appliance, Cloudflare One, Cloudflare WAN - Define custom applications for breakout and prioritized traffic from the Cloudflare One Appliance dashboard
item.description:
You can now define custom applications for breakout and prioritized traffic on the Cloudflare One Appliance directly from the dashboard, without calling the API.

  • In Traffic Steering > Breakout traffic or Prioritized traffic, select Assign application traffic > Add to create a custom application matched by Hostnames, IP subnets, and/or the new Source subnets field, alongside Cloudflare-managed applications.
  • Edit or delete an existing custom application from the same panel, no API round-trip required.
  • Source subnets lets you match traffic by its source IP range, complementing the existing source LAN interface breakout criteria.

This complements the existing API and Terraform workflow for managing applications.

For details, refer to Breakout traffic and Prioritized traffic.

item.title: Cloudflare One Appliance, Cloudflare One, Cloudflare WAN - Configure DHCP options from the dashboard on Cloudflare One Appliance
item.description:
You can now configure custom DHCP options directly from the dashboard when the Cloudflare One Appliance is acting as the DHCP server for a LAN.

  • In LAN configuration, under DHCP server options, select Add DHCP option to choose from common options for PXE / iPXE boot, VoIP phone provisioning, and vendor-specific configuration, or select Add custom option to enter your own option code, type, and value.
  • This complements the existing API and Terraform workflow for configuring DHCP options.

For details, refer to DHCP server options.

item.title: Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare One, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Mesh - Create multiple Cloudflare Tunnel and Cloudflare Mesh routes at once
item.description:
You can now create multiple Cloudflare Tunnel and Cloudflare Mesh routes from the Routes page in a single action, instead of submitting one route at a time.

When creating a route, you can now:

  • Add multiple destinations at once — Enter a comma-separated list of CIDR ranges or hostnames to create several routes of the same type and connector together.
  • Queue up multiple routes — Select Add another to stage additional routes, including different types or connectors, before creating them all in one action.
  • Retry only what failed — If some routes in a batch fail (for example, an invalid CIDR), the routes that were created successfully are removed from the form automatically, so you only need to fix and resubmit the ones that failed.

The same Routes UI already supports bulk creation for Cloudflare WAN static routes, so you can add multiple WAN destinations or queue up several WAN routes before creating them together as well.

Go to Routes ↗

For setup steps, refer to Add routes.

item.title: Access - Access service token secrets use a scannable format
item.description:
Cloudflare Access service token Client Secrets created on or after August 26, 2026, use the format cfast_[40 alphanumeric characters][8-character checksum]. The prefix and checksum make these credentials easier for secret scanning tools to identify with fewer false positives.

Existing service token secrets continue to work and do not require rotation. Both formats use the same Client ID and the same CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret authentication headers.

For more information, refer to Service tokens.

item.title: Access - Grace periods for service token rotation
item.description:
Cloudflare Access administrators can now choose a grace period when rotating a service token secret. Both secrets remain valid during the grace period, giving administrators time to update services without interrupting authentication.

The dashboard offers grace periods from one hour to 30 days. Administrators can also revoke the previous secret immediately. The API accepts an RFC 3339 expiration time for custom rotation schedules.

For configuration instructions, refer to Rotate service token secrets.

item.title: Access - Temporarily turn off Access service tokens
item.description:
Cloudflare Access administrators can now temporarily turn off service tokens without deleting them. A disabled token cannot authenticate, but its configuration remains available so administrators can turn it on again later.

Turning off a token also stops any previous secret in an active rotation grace period. Use this control to contain suspected credential exposure or pause an automated service.

For configuration instructions, refer to Turn a service token on or off.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Access - MCP server portals support MCP 2026-07-28 specification
item.description:
MCP server portals support the stateless MCP 2026-07-28 specification for client and upstream server connections.

The portal's /mcp endpoint automatically accepts stateless MCP 2026-07-28 requests and earlier 2025 Streamable HTTP clients. When the portal connects to an upstream Streamable HTTP server, it checks for MCP 2026-07-28 support and falls back to the 2025 handshake when needed. Client and upstream protocol selection are independent, so clients and servers can upgrade separately without portal configuration changes.

SSE connections continue to use the legacy protocol. For details, refer to MCP server portal transport and protocol compatibility.

item.title: Cloudflare One Appliance, Cloudflare One, Cloudflare WAN - Download the Cloudflare One Virtual Appliance for your hypervisor from the dashboard
item.description:
When you register a Cloudflare One Virtual Appliance, you can now select your hypervisor and download the appliance directly from the dashboard — no need to look up asset URLs.

  • On the Connectors page, select Add an appliance, choose Virtual appliance, then select your hypervisor: VMware ESXi, Proxmox, or libvirt/KVM.
  • Download the OVA image (VMware ESXi) or the install script (Proxmox and libvirt/KVM) for the selected hypervisor.
  • Use View setup guide to open deployment instructions for your platform.

This complements the existing self-serve registration and license key generation in the dashboard.

For details, refer to Configure a Cloudflare One Virtual Appliance.

item.title: CASB - Automatically remediate Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace findings with API-based CASB remediation policies
item.description:
Cloudflare CASB is an API-based (agentless) tool that continuously scans your SaaS and cloud applications for security misconfigurations and data exposure. You can now use CASB remediation policies to automatically fix a finding or send a webhook the moment CASB detects it, without manual triage.

Remediate Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace findings

A policy can perform a first-party remediation action directly against the SaaS integration API. When a policy triggers, Cloudflare revokes the external sharing configuration without human intervention.

Remediation is currently supported for file-sharing findings in Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. Support for additional finding types and integrations is coming soon. For the full list of supported finding types, refer to Run remediations in the CASB remediation policies documentation.

Send webhooks

A policy can send posture finding data to Slack, ServiceNow, or any other webhook destination. Webhook actions are supported for all posture finding types across CASB integrations.

A single policy can perform both actions: remediate a finding and send a webhook.

Get started

  1. In Cloudflare One ↗︎, go to Cloud & SaaS findings > Policies.
  2. Select Create a policy.
  3. Under Basic information, enter a Policy name and, optionally, a Description.
  4. Under Choose how you want to trigger the policy, select a Vendor, Integration, and Finding type.
  5. Under Define what to do with findings that match your trigger, choose Run Remediation, Send webhooks, or both.
  6. Under Status, turn on Enable policy.
  7. Select Create policy.

Learn more

  • Learn how to create and manage CASB remediation policies in Cloudflare One.
  • Configure CASB webhooks as a policy destination.
  • Learn how to manage findings in Cloudflare One.

CASB remediation policies are now available in Cloudflare One.

item.title: Data Loss Prevention - Test Data Loss Prevention profiles without sending traffic through Gateway
item.description:
Test scan lets you check how Data Loss Prevention (DLP) evaluates sample content before you apply a profile to production traffic. Paste text, upload a file, or upload a HAR file, then select the profiles you want to test.

Test scan sends content directly to the DLP scanner. Gateway policies are not evaluated, no traffic passes through Gateway, and no Gateway activity logs are created. Results include matched profiles, detection entries, confidence levels, match context, proximity keywords, file metadata, antivirus status, and OCR output.

Test scan is available to all Cloudflare Zero Trust customers. Profile availability depends on your Zero Trust plan.

For more details, refer to the Test scan documentation.

item.title: Cloudflare One Client - Cloudflare One Client for Windows (version 2026.7.1343.0)
item.description:
A new GA release for the Windows Cloudflare One Client is now available on the stable releases downloads page.

This release introduces multiple features from our previous beta release into stable release, including:

  • When reauthentication is needed for any reason, the notifications are clearer and reduce the actions needed to get you back to work by redirecting to the browser for authentication instead of the app window when necessary.
  • When a network is blocking or otherwise not supportive of HTTP/3, the client will learn and adapt by switching the order of fallback for that network by starting with HTTP/2 first and then trying HTTP/3 if needed. This reduces delays in time to connectivity when joining older or heavily filtered networks.

Additional changes and improvements

  • Fixed a process leak in the Windows GUI that could exhaust system resources during IPC client-creation failures.
  • Fixed being unable to switch organizations when the client was stuck in the "Device not in organization" state.
  • Fixed an issue where Microsoft Defender would falsely flag the Cloudflare One Client installation as malicious when installing with Intune.
  • Made the Windows domain-joined posture check more reliable.
  • A DNS search domain parsing failure no longer prevents connection.
  • Cloud icon now correctly reflects actual connection status instead of showing disconnected while fully connected.
  • Fixed missing certificate error display due to a race condition.
  • Fixed empty black window after transitioning from docked dual displays to undocked/internal display.

Known issues

  • If a user upgrades to version 2026.7.1343.0, downgrades to an earlier version, re-registers, and then upgrades back to 2026.7.1343.0, the client might fail to connect or switch organizations. To resolve this issue, run warp-cli registration delete or warp-cli registration delete-all.

item.title: Access, Cloudflare Fundamentals - Access resource lists now support resource-scoped roles
item.description:
Members with only resource-scoped Access roles can now open Access resource list pages in the Cloudflare dashboard and call list endpoints in the API. They no longer need an additional account-scoped read-only role to list resources.

The dashboard and API return only resources included in the member's permission policy scopes. Filtering applies to Access applications, policies, service tokens, and identity providers. This allows administrators to delegate specific Access resources without granting account-wide visibility. Previously, the dashboard blocked these list pages and API list requests returned 403 responses.

For members with the Cloudflare Access App Admin role, policy lists include policies attached directly to the selected application. Reusable policies appear only when the member has the Cloudflare Access Policy Admin role for those policies.

For role definitions and assignment details, refer to Resource-scoped roles and Role scopes.
